top.title: South Carolina Basketball Suffers First Loss Of The Season In Thriller
top.description: Photo by: Jeff Blake South Carolina basketball came within a few possessions of pulling off an impressive upset Wednesday afternoon, but the Gamecocks ultimately fell 71-69 to No. 18 USC in the Acrisure Series in Palm Desert, California. The Gamecocks entered the matchup undefeated at 5-0 and faced their biggest challenge of the young season against a talented USC team. South Carolina controlled much of the contest, held a halftime lead and appeared to be in position to hand the Trojans their first loss. However, USC found a way to turn things around late, using a decisive run in the final minutes to escape with the victory. With the loss, South Carolina dropped to 5-1, while USC improved to 7-0 and kept its perfect record intact. Gamecocks Set the Tone Early South Carolina came out ready to compete, showing it was not intimidated by the nationally ranked Trojans. The Gamecocks used strong outside shooting to keep USC’s defense off balance. Camden Heide was especially effective from beyond the arc, knocking down four three pointers and finishing with 12 points. Aleksas Bieliauskas also delivered a major performance inside. The forward scored 18 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, giving South Carolina an important presence on both ends of the floor. The Gamecocks built an early advantage and continued making shots throughout the opening half. Their three-point shooting helped them stay ahead of USC’s high powered offense. South Carolina entered halftime with a 37-35 lead, putting itself in a strong position to compete for another important victory. South Carolina Holds Its Ground After Halftime The second half featured plenty of back and forth action, with South Carolina continuing to find ways to slow down the Trojans. USC entered the game averaging more than 94 points per contest, but the Gamecocks did a strong job limiting its offensive production. The Trojans struggled from the field and particularly had trouble finding their rhythm from three point range. Alijah Arenas became the biggest offensive weapon for USC. He finished with a game-high 25 points and consistently found opportunities to attack the basket and get to the free throw line. Rodney Rice added 13 points, although he struggled with his shooting and finished with five turnovers. South Carolina continued to lead for much of the afternoon and built a 10 point advantage with just over eight minutes remaining. At that point, the Gamecocks appeared to be closing in on a major upset. USC Delivers Late Comeback Unfortunately for South Carolina, the final minutes belonged to the Trojans. USC increased its defensive pressure and began taking advantage of opportunities at the free-throw line. The Trojans closed the game on a 10-2 run, holding the Gamecocks scoreless over the final 4:05. South Carolina had opportunities to regain the lead, but late missed shots prevented the Gamecocks from completing the upset. Arenas led the comeback and finished 12 of 13 from the free throw line. top.title: Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears preview: 4 key stats
top.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions attempts to sack Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears during an NFL football game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The two most recent NFC North division champions pitted against each other to kick off the NFL’s Thanksgiving spectacular. Both teams are 8-2 in loaded divisional and conference races. Dan Campbell vs. Ben Johnson. This is why the NFL is undefeated. One of the few hurdles Campbell has yet to clear is finding consistent success on Turkey Day. After going 1-5 on Thanksgiving as a player with the Lions and Dallas Cowboys, Campbell is just 1-4 as the Lions’ head coach in their annual spotlight game. Detroit is 1-8 on Thanksgiving over the last nine seasons, with the Chicago Bears alone going 3-1 against the Lions in that span. The Lions have endured a grueling stretch, returning from Germany and playing last week without the luxury of a bye, followed by this short four-day turnaround. However, this game carries more weight than any they’ve played since their back-to-back divisional matchups against the Packers and Vikings. As a reminder, the Lions will play all three of their road divisional games over the last four games, making it even more imperative that they take care of business at home. This week’s Lions-Bears preview will focus on both sides of the ball, with a heightened emphasis on how defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s burgeoning defensive unit can turn Bears QB Caleb Williams into a turducken. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Can’t Run Away From Your Problems The Bears’ offense this season hasn’t quite reached the heights of efficiency it attained at times last year, except Week 1, when it put together a 59-burger firework factory against the Panthers. In fact, while the Bears haven’t trailed since Williams returned to the lineup in Week 6, their offense has averaged just -0.04 EPA/play in that span, good for a clean league-average ranking of 16th. One area that’s had hiccups in that span is the run game, which has suffered from the downgrade of center Drew Dalman (offseason retirement) to Garrett Bradbury and the loss of tight end Cole Kmet to injured reserve, a rock-fighting Geodude on the perimeter. The Bears are still committed to running the football, with a 46.8% run rate (8th), but where they’re really struggling is on early downs, putting themselves behind the eight ball. Since Week 6, their 132 early-down (first- and second-down) rushing attempts have generated just 3.3 yards/rush (29th), -0.269 EPA/rush (32nd), and a 34.1% success rate (27th). That’s not the run-game wagon Ben Johnson, one of football’s better run-game architects, had rolling last year. top.title: James becomes oldest with NBA triple-double in Sixers win
top.description: LeBron James of the Philadelphia 76ers became the oldest NBA player to produce a triple double at barely a month before his 42nd birthday in a victory over the Miami Heat (Mitchell Leff) LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over Miami in the NBA Cup on Wednesday. Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player James, who turns 42 on December 30, scored a season-high 25 points, passed off a season-high 12 assists and pulled down 10 rebounds for the 76ers. Miami grabbed a 32-29 lead after the first quarter, but James scored 14 consecutive Sixers points in a second-quarter run for a 62-53 halftime lead, and the hosts never lost the lead in the second half. "We wanted to get back to our defensive identity," James said. "We didn't do that in the first quarter but for the next 36 minutes I thought we got back to that." The 76ers improved the best record in the Eastern Conference to 15-4 while snapping a seven-game win streak for Miami (10-7). Both clubs are 2-1 in East Group B Cup play, but with a win Miami would have clinched the group and advanced to the knockout stage of the in-season tournament. With Joel Embiid out due to illness and Jaylen Brown out after early left hamstring tightness, it fell to James to score and set up his teammates with NFL-ish passing. "That's my favorite aspect of my game besides my IQ," James said. "So to be able to go out there and just play like a quarterback role and watch these guys run the right routes and it's my job to put it on time and on target, it was fun." Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 30 points while fellow guard VJ Edgecombe added 18. "In this league you have to have some depth for sure," James said. "It's a fast-paced game. It feels good for us. These are my young bulls right here. They keep me going. They keep me energized." Greek star Giannis Antetokounmpo led Miami with 32 points and 14 rebounds. A late rebound gave James his first triple double with the 76ers, drawing a standing ovation from the Philadelphia crowd. James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the off-season and selected the 76ers from several clubs in hopes of capturing a fifth NBA crown. js/pnb

top.description: St. John's Red Storm forward Ruben Prey (17) and Siena Saints guard Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) fight for a loose ball in Queens, N.Y., Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. LAS VEGAS — The top priority is pretty obvious for St. John’s on Thanksgiving night: rebounding, rebounding and more rebounding. Access the St. John's beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Zach Braziller about the inside buzz on St. John’s. TRY IT NOW That was coach Rick Pitino’s biggest concern this week in Sin City, and the 13th-ranked Johnnies will have to deal with one of the best offensive rebounding teams in the country in No. 25 Louisville. Led by twin towers Flory Bidunga and Obinna Ekezie Jr., the Cardinals are seventh nationally in offensive rebounding percentage at 44.6. They hammered No. 5 Texas Tech on the glass, 41-28, in their Tuesday night opener of the Players Era Festival. “It’s a big focus for sure. They get [almost] 50 percent of their misses back,” Red Storm big man Ruben Prey said Wednesday. “We have to make that number lower.” Red Storm forward Ruben Prey (17) and Saints guard Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) fight for a loose ball during the St. John’s blowout win over Siena on Nov. 18, 2026, at Carnesecca Arena. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect St. John’s is familiar with the 6-foot-9 Bidunga. The Red Storm faced him in the second round of the NCAA Tournament last March while he was with Kansas . The Red Storm did a strong job in the rebounding department Tuesday against Oregon . They were plus-4 on the boards and limited Oregon big man Malique Ewin to seven points and four rebounds. Prey outplayed him, finishing with 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. The guards rebounded well, as Quinn Ellis, Ian Jackson and Tounde Yessoufou combined for 18 boards. But Louisville is a different animal. The Cardinals will play Bidunga and the 7-foot-2 Ekezie Jr. together at times. The onus will be on the 6-foot-11 Prey to protect the interior. “I feel like it can still get some improvement,” Prey said of his rebounding. “I’m not totally happy with it. But I also am happy with my improvement during the season. I’ve been getting better, and I will continue to improve.” Babacar Sane is still spending more time watching than playing. The athletically gifted forward from Senegal remains a work in progress. Pitino has had a short leash with the 6-foot-7 Sane after turnovers or missed defensive assignments. He was limited to six minutes Tuesday. “I think he’s handling it like a professional,” Jackson said. “He’s been great. Obviously, it’s not the easiest thing to do. He’s approached it well. He’s coming out looking out for ways to get better, looking to understand what he’s doing wrong, looking to fix it. It’s really nice to watch: an older guy being able to handle something like that.”

Both players were outstanding prospects, but Glenn said the Jets saw Bailey’s ability to rush the passer as a separator. “I’m a huge believer in, you build a team from the inside out and when you have someone of the magnitude that you know has a chance to affect the game by affecting the quarterback,” Glenn said, “which at the end, if you can affect the quarterback, man, that makes a huge difference in winning and losing. So, that was a huge part of the decision-making of getting a guy that can affect the quarterback and he is a front-line guy. That actually just went into our philosophy in general and I love the pick. I think he’s doing a great job. A lot of things that he can improve on, but that’s the reason why.” David Bailey looks on before the Jets’ loss to the Bills on Nov. 15, 2026 at MetLife Stadium. Getty Images Bailey has played very well for the Jets and has a team-best 9 ½ sacks. He is on the verge of setting the franchise record for sacks by a rookie. Hugh Douglas owns the mark with 10 in 1995. He also has a shot at the NFL rookie record of 14 ½ by Jevon Kearse with the 1999 Titans. Bailey stands out for his play and his style. He does not wear gloves or wristbands and does not celebrate sacks. “I mean, it’s kind of weird when you see it on tape, especially coming out of college because everyone has five towels, everyone has six, seven wristbands on, but I get it,” Glenn said. “Some people say you look good, play good, but I guess that’s what he looks good doing because he damn sure plays good for us. top.title: MLB sues players union to boost lockout as deadline looms
top.description: Major League Baseball sued its players union in New York, hoping to secure protection from antitrust complaints in the wake of a lockout as a deadline looms to sign a new collective bargaining agreement (Mark Brown) Major League Baseball filed a lawsuit against the MLB Players Association on Wednesday seeking legal protection for a lockout expected to begin next week when their current collective bargaining agreement expires. The complaint filed in US District Court in New York seeks a declaration that a lockout would be legal under US antitrust law. The move would safeguard MLB if the players give up union status and try to sue MLB under antitrust law, exposing the league to potentially greater damages. MLB team owners have said they will not accept any new deal without a salary cap, a system the players union has successfully fought for decades. With a Tuesday deadline fast approaching, the lawsuit raised the stakes as both sides fought to determine how to divide billions of dollars in profits. "Today's filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. "We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to 'disclaim' its status as the players' bargaining representative to pursue an antitrust lawsuit as an end run around the bargaining process. "We have asked a federal court in the Southern District of New York to proactively disarm the union's nuclear option of disclaiming." MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer called the lawsuit "completely frivolous" in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing." js/pnb

top.title: Los Angeles Rams vs. Green Bay Packers, Thanksgiving Eve game chat
top.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during a game against the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium on October 06, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the NFL went and found reason to schedule a game on a Wednesday, crowning what’s certain to become it’s own brand of holiday with what’s been dubbed “The Thanksgiving Eve” game. In the early decades of the NFL preceding the 1940s — back when lights on funny looking cars, street lamps, and those indoors were still sometimes powered by oil and kerosene, and a short while later by carbide gas — Wednesday games were not unusual. Since 1940? Before tonight, six NFL games of notoriety were played on a Wednesday in the last 86 years, and none from 1949 through 2011. Do you know when the most recent game was played before this evening’s matchup? September 22, 1948: Los Angeles Rams vs. Detroit Lions (First Wednesday game after 1940) September 5, 2012: Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants (Moved from Thursday to avoid President Obama’s DNC speech) December 2, 2020: Baltimore Ravens vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (COVID-19-rescheduled game) December 25, 2024: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Steelers (Christmas Day game) December 25, 2024: Ravens vs. Houston Texans (Christmas Day game) September 9, 2026: Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots (2026 NFL season opener ahead of Thursday game in Australia) Yesterday’s NFL is not today’s NFL, and with each of today’s games put in front of scores of holiday eyes, new interest grows. The move lately has been to put juicy matchups in the best slots of each major holiday. But tonight? This evening, the Los Angeles Rams, Green Bay Packers, and the NFL get a new “holiday” all to themselves. Okay, maybe they’ll have to fight for the attention of people out at informal high school reunions, but you know the game’s going to be on even at Applebee’s. (The impetus for that behemoth’s name is as thrilling as you might guess.) But here we are as a species, soaking in every single second of NFL football available to us. Truth be told, tonight’s game has real potential to be great. Two 6-4 teams are fighting to remain in playoff contention, with Green Bay hanging on to the seventh (and last) seed in the current NFL playoff race. If the regular season ended today, the Rams would be watching the postseason from home as the ninth seed in the NFC. Rooting interests? It’s another NFC-NFC game, so nothing carries too much weight. Additionally, the Bills already played the Rams and will play the Packers Week 14 — that means no real advantage by having one win over other for strength of schedule benefits. Hoping to watch the game? You’ll need a Netflix or NFL+ subscription. Here’s your open thread for the first-ever “Thanksgiving Eve” NFL game. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things, Go Bills!

top.title: Syracuse 74, Albany 53: Orange go 2-3 zone to defeat Great Danes
top.description: Nov 25, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange forward Sadiq White Jr. (1) and UAlbany Great Danes guard Abdoulaye Fall (7) battle for the ball during the first half at the JMA Wireless Dome. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SYRACUSE, N.Y. — It was shades of Syracuse past on Wednesday night. After being deadlocked for much of the night with the Albany Great Danes, Syracuse needed to go to a 2-3 zone to put away its in-state opponent by a final score of 74-53 from the JMA Wireless Dome. It was the second game in a row in which Gerry McNamara had to go to a different defense to change the tenor of the game. Syracuse (5-2) was led by Abdramane Siby’s 17 points on 8-8 shooting. Sadiq White once again posted a double-double with 10 points and 11 rebounds. Ryan Moesch flirted with a triple-double, going for 13 points, 9 rebounds, 8 assists and 4 steals. Albany (4-5) was led by Ollie Engen’s 23 points. Syracuse had a 44-26 points in the paint advantage and the Orange bench out-scored Albany’s 33-16. Moesch made his second career start with Garwey Dual sidelined with an ankle injury . Aiden Tobiason remained sidelined with a hamstring injury but did go through warmups. Siby checked in first off the bench and got things started in the scoring column for the Orange on a dunk. Syracuse showed press early, going to a 1-2-2 as the Orange jumped out to an 8-2 lead. Sadiq White picked up two early fouls, however, and had to sit for extended time on the Syracuse bench. Amarri Monroe checked in for White and Kiyan Anthony rounded out the rotation off the bench. Anthony and Moesch scored back to back transitions layups as Syracuse went up 13-8. Albany responded with a 10-2 run to retake the lead 18-15. A frustrated McNamara called timeout at the 8:32 mark. Displeased with his starting and backup center, McNamara inserted Tasman Goodrick into the game to man the middle. Goodrick would close out the half with Luke Wilson and Siby on the bench. White returned back into the game with his two fouls at the six minutes mark in the first half. He’d finish a transition lob for a layup and was one of the few Orange players bringing energy in the first half. Both teams struggled mightily on offense in the first and went into the break tied at 26. Syracuse and Albany both shot 31% from the floor. Syracuse turned it over 12 times in the first half to Albany’s eight. The scoring picked up on both ends out of the half. Syracuse went inside to Wilson and Albany responded inside before Mark Morano connected on back-to-back threes. White picked up two quick fouls and had to return to the bench at the 17:02 mark, his fourth a questionable call after some embellishing on Albany’s Pedro Santos. After replay review, the call was reversed as Santos was called for the foul while White’s fourth foul was wiped away. White stayed in the game with three personal fouls. The Aggies entered the matchup at 6-0 and were looking to continue building momentum after an impressive start to the season. However, Xavier proved to be a difficult challenge, using strong rebounding and timely offensive runs to take control of the game. Texas A&M battled back from a significant deficit and made things interesting late, but the Musketeers delivered when it mattered most to secure the five-point victory. With the loss, the Aggies dropped to 6-1, while Xavier improved to 6-1 and advanced in the tournament. PJ Haggerty led Texas A&M with 18 points, continuing his strong start to the season. Jalen Shelley also provided an important contribution with 16 points. Xavier Builds an Early Advantage The Musketeers came out aggressively and took advantage of Texas A&M’s early mistakes. Turnovers and fouls created problems for the Aggies, allowing Xavier to establish control during the opening minutes. Xavier eventually built a double-digit advantage, leading 34-22 with eight minutes remaining in the first half. Texas A&M responded with a strong finish to the period. Haggerty helped get the offense moving, and the Aggies closed the half on an 8-0 run. A three-pointer from Josh Irving capped the stretch and brought Texas A&M within four points. The Musketeers pushed the advantage to 18 points at one stage, putting the Aggies in a difficult position. However, Texas A&M refused to give up. The Aggies turned up their defensive pressure and began forcing turnovers with their high-pressure defense. Those mistakes created opportunities in transition and helped Texas A&M work its way back into the contest. Haggerty continued leading the offensive attack, while Shelley provided a major spark. top.title: Pennridge-Quakertown game postponed; Bristol-Morrisville cancelled
top.description: The 97th annual Pennridge - Quakertown Thanksgiving football game was postponed to Saturday morning due to the expected heavy rain on Thursday. top.title: Rams versus Packers live discussion: We’re all cheeseheads tonight
top.description: The seventh-seeded Green Bay Packers take on the 9th-seeded Los Angeles Rams. That is not something you would have thought would be true about these two teams at this point in the season if somebody had told you that in August. The Packers hold the tiebreaker over the Rams, thanks to a better conference record. This is a matchup the Packers have dominated. Against the Rams, Green Bay is 20-2 in their last 22 games. They are 10-1 in the last 11. When you own a team to that extent, it’s no longer a trend. It’s domination. Green Bay has fared pretty well in their last dozen contests against the NFC West in general. It’s odd, but it can’t be ignored. The Rams are without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. That hasn’t slowed down the Rams during the past month, as they still rank sixth in the league in EPA per play and success rate. But they’ve faced the Cardinals twice, the Commanders, Chargers, and Raiders since Week 6. The last time they faced a top offense was in Week 5, and the Bills scored 37 points. To their credit, the Rams have been stingy defensively. Only one team has scored more than 18 points since the Bills game. They’ve dictated much of the game, but this will be an offense that can truly challenge the Rams in ways they haven’t been all season. The Packers are one of those “all-or-nothing” kind of offenses. They can go multiple drives without scoring, and then hit on a big play or three to flip the scoreboard. This should be a lower-scoring game. It probably won’t be fun to watch. History says the Packers will win. Micah Parsons is back, and that should make it a living hell for Matthew Stafford, who has been off all season. Packers 24, Rams 21.

nigeria.title: Awka City chosen for AfDB -funded Action Plan for Africa’s coordinated urban development
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Awka, the capital city of Anambra State, has been selected for the African Development Bank, AfDB, – funded action plan for coordinated urban development in Africa. Under the programme, government would provide the policy direction, regulatory clarity, and institutional leadership, while development partners would support the mobilisation of technical expertise and catalytic resources. Also, the private sector is expected to play a decisive role in financing and delivering viable infrastructure and urban projects, traditional institutions, community leaders, professional bodies and residents will remain vital in safeguarding public ownership and ensuring that development stays centred on the people in the new city. At the launch of the plan on Wednesday in Awka, the state governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo said it is part of the strategic plan to create the envisioned Anambra mega city. Represented by his special Adviser on trade and commerce, Mr. Christian Udechukwu, the governor recalled that Awka is the only city chosen in Africa for the project, noting that it is because of the long term vision and the strategic implementation and the intentionality and purposeful focus of the administration. According to Udechukwu, it is the governor’s determination to transform Anambra State that drew the attention of the African Development Bank to the state. “The reforms they see here are of significance that it would serve to use Awka City as a model to prove the sustainability of the project and we are happy that this is happening under this administration”, he said. He said that a substantial amount of next year’s budget would be devoted to the development of the new Awka City, while other cities of Onitsha, Nnewi, and Ekwulobia would also undergo transformation, in addition to the new cities planned for the state. “When Awka 2.0 joins the planned industrial city, the proposed axis of prosperity would have been created. So Anambra is being positioned to become the economic hub of Nigeria and that is why the selection of Awka as a primary model sustainable city in Africa is important to us as a government. We should therefore not waste more time to move into the project preparatory stage”, Udechukwu said. Speaking at the launch, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Awka Capital Territory Development Authority, ACTDA, Dr Osita Onuko said the coordinated development framework is aimed at addressing the growing infrastructure and environmental challenges confronting Awka and guiding the capital city’s expansion towards a more liveable and inclusive future. nigeria.title: Malen penalty ends PSG’s perfect UCL run as Roma snatch 2-2 draw
nigeria.description: Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end. Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute on a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, giving Roma a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out. Roma had earlier taken the lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to equalise before substitute Ousmane Dembele put PSG briefly in front with a penalty of his own. The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team. They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches. It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the play-off round like in the last two campaigns. But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness too and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result. Dembele’s presence on the bench at kick-off meant that none of PSG’s five top scorers from last season were in their line-up here, with the others either injured or having departed in the case of Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos. Meanwhile, Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini raised eyebrows by leaving Malen out of his starting XI. The Dutchman is running at an average of more than a goal a game this season and netted four against Parma last weekend. – Dembele spot-kick – However, Roma have been in prolific form in general, netting 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in the French capital. They went ahead inside five minutes here as Matias Soule cut the ball back from the byline and Spanish defender Hermoso was on hand to convert. Roma had blown even more promising leads already this season, though, losing 4-3 at home to Real Madrid after leading 3-1 with eight minutes left, and then going down 3-2 at Old Trafford despite being 2-0 ahead at half-time. nigeria.title: UCL: Pochettino still winless as Man United draw 2-2 with Sporting
nigeria.description: Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side. United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half. Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game. United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match. A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick. Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha. Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control. Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty. The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later. Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot. – United unhappy with disallowed goals – United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay. Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded. Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez. The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner. Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season. The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch. nigeria.title: Dangote Refinery to list on Nigerian Exchange December 1
nigeria.description: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery says it will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) Group on December 1, marking its entry into the Nigerian stock market following its initial public offering (IPO). Devakumar Edwin, vice-president of oil and gas at Dangote Group, announced the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s share allocation plan following its heavily oversubscribed IPO, which closed last month. The regulatory approval cleared the way for the company to distribute shares to investors and proceed with preparations for its stock market debut. The refinery had earlier sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong investor demand. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, president of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), said the refinery planned to pursue a listing on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, Africa’s richest person said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and globally. nigeria.title: Troops rescue 5 kidnapped victims, arrest 2 suspected terrorists in Kaduna

nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. nigeria.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. nigeria.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
nigeria.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. nigeria.title: Nigeria needs experienced, courageous leaders to tackle challenges, Amaechi hails Atiku at 80
nigeria.description: Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, saying Nigeria needs leaders with the experience, courage and capacity to address its economic and security challenges. Amaechi, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, described Atiku as a distinguished statesman, entrepreneur, philanthropist and patriot whose contributions to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development remained significant. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), turned 80 on Wednesday. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State, recalled Atiku’s tenure as Vice President between 1999 and 2007, noting his role in consolidating the Fourth Republic and driving economic reforms. He also highlighted Atiku’s leadership of the National Council on Privatisation, saying his contributions reflected his belief in private-sector development and an enabling business environment. The former minister also commended Atiku’s entrepreneurial investments in agriculture, logistics and real estate, as well as his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola. He said the university reflected Atiku’s commitment to education and human capital development. Amaechi further acknowledged Atiku’s philanthropic activities, particularly his support for educational opportunities for disadvantaged Nigerians and young people affected by the Chibok tragedy. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Amaechi said Nigeria required leadership capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening national security, improving education and healthcare, and ensuring reliable electricity supply. He also backed Atiku’s proposed reintroduction of petroleum production subsidy, arguing that the policy could reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices on households. According to Amaechi, Nigeria needs a people-centred development agenda that prioritises entrepreneurship, technological innovation, human capital development and private-sector-led growth. He expressed confidence in Atiku’s ambition to contest the 2027 presidential election, saying the country needed leaders who understood its challenges and were prepared to take difficult decisions. Amaechi also called for a Nigeria where young people could find opportunities at home, farmers could prosper, businesses could grow and citizens could access quality education regardless of their backgrounds. He wished Atiku good health, wisdom and strength, while commending his contributions to public service, education, philanthropy and the country’s democratic development. “At 80, your journey is not merely a story of past accomplishments but a reminder that experience must be deployed in the service of the future,” Amaechi said. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. Changes from Begich’s original version The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts. Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. sports.title: James becomes oldest with NBA triple-double in Sixers win
sports.description: LeBron James of the Philadelphia 76ers became the oldest NBA player to produce a triple double at barely a month before his 42nd birthday in a victory over the Miami Heat (Mitchell Leff) LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over Miami in the NBA Cup on Wednesday. Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player James, who turns 42 on December 30, scored a season-high 25 points, passed off a season-high 12 assists and pulled down 10 rebounds for the 76ers. Miami grabbed a 32-29 lead after the first quarter, but James scored 14 consecutive Sixers points in a second-quarter run for a 62-53 halftime lead, and the hosts never lost the lead in the second half. "We wanted to get back to our defensive identity," James said. "We didn't do that in the first quarter but for the next 36 minutes I thought we got back to that." The 76ers improved the best record in the Eastern Conference to 15-4 while snapping a seven-game win streak for Miami (10-7). Both clubs are 2-1 in East Group B Cup play, but with a win Miami would have clinched the group and advanced to the knockout stage of the in-season tournament. With Joel Embiid out due to illness and Jaylen Brown out after early left hamstring tightness, it fell to James to score and set up his teammates with NFL-ish passing. "That's my favorite aspect of my game besides my IQ," James said. "So to be able to go out there and just play like a quarterback role and watch these guys run the right routes and it's my job to put it on time and on target, it was fun." Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 30 points while fellow guard VJ Edgecombe added 18. "In this league you have to have some depth for sure," James said. "It's a fast-paced game. It feels good for us. These are my young bulls right here. They keep me going. They keep me energized." Greek star Giannis Antetokounmpo led Miami with 32 points and 14 rebounds. A late rebound gave James his first triple double with the 76ers, drawing a standing ovation from the Philadelphia crowd. James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the off-season and selected the 76ers from several clubs in hopes of capturing a fifth NBA crown. js/pnb

sports.title: MLB sues players union to boost lockout as deadline looms
sports.description: Major League Baseball sued its players union in New York, hoping to secure protection from antitrust complaints in the wake of a lockout as a deadline looms to sign a new collective bargaining agreement (Mark Brown) Major League Baseball filed a lawsuit against the MLB Players Association on Wednesday seeking legal protection for a lockout expected to begin next week when their current collective bargaining agreement expires. The complaint filed in US District Court in New York seeks a declaration that a lockout would be legal under US antitrust law. The move would safeguard MLB if the players give up union status and try to sue MLB under antitrust law, exposing the league to potentially greater damages. MLB team owners have said they will not accept any new deal without a salary cap, a system the players union has successfully fought for decades. With a Tuesday deadline fast approaching, the lawsuit raised the stakes as both sides fought to determine how to divide billions of dollars in profits. "Today's filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. "We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to 'disclaim' its status as the players' bargaining representative to pursue an antitrust lawsuit as an end run around the bargaining process. "We have asked a federal court in the Southern District of New York to proactively disarm the union's nuclear option of disclaiming." MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer called the lawsuit "completely frivolous" in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing." js/pnb

sports.title: Los Angeles Rams vs. Green Bay Packers, Thanksgiving Eve game chat
sports.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during a game against the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium on October 06, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the NFL went and found reason to schedule a game on a Wednesday, crowning what’s certain to become it’s own brand of holiday with what’s been dubbed “The Thanksgiving Eve” game. In the early decades of the NFL preceding the 1940s — back when lights on funny looking cars, street lamps, and those indoors were still sometimes powered by oil and kerosene, and a short while later by carbide gas — Wednesday games were not unusual. Since 1940? Before tonight, six NFL games of notoriety were played on a Wednesday in the last 86 years, and none from 1949 through 2011. Do you know when the most recent game was played before this evening’s matchup? September 22, 1948: Los Angeles Rams vs. Detroit Lions (First Wednesday game after 1940) September 5, 2012: Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants (Moved from Thursday to avoid President Obama’s DNC speech) December 2, 2020: Baltimore Ravens vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (COVID-19-rescheduled game) December 25, 2024: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Steelers (Christmas Day game) December 25, 2024: Ravens vs. Houston Texans (Christmas Day game) September 9, 2026: Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots (2026 NFL season opener ahead of Thursday game in Australia) Yesterday’s NFL is not today’s NFL, and with each of today’s games put in front of scores of holiday eyes, new interest grows. The move lately has been to put juicy matchups in the best slots of each major holiday. But tonight? This evening, the Los Angeles Rams, Green Bay Packers, and the NFL get a new “holiday” all to themselves. Okay, maybe they’ll have to fight for the attention of people out at informal high school reunions, but you know the game’s going to be on even at Applebee’s. (The impetus for that behemoth’s name is as thrilling as you might guess.) But here we are as a species, soaking in every single second of NFL football available to us. Truth be told, tonight’s game has real potential to be great. Two 6-4 teams are fighting to remain in playoff contention, with Green Bay hanging on to the seventh (and last) seed in the current NFL playoff race. If the regular season ended today, the Rams would be watching the postseason from home as the ninth seed in the NFC. Rooting interests? It’s another NFC-NFC game, so nothing carries too much weight. Additionally, the Bills already played the Rams and will play the Packers Week 14 — that means no real advantage by having one win over other for strength of schedule benefits. Hoping to watch the game? You’ll need a Netflix or NFL+ subscription. Here’s your open thread for the first-ever “Thanksgiving Eve” NFL game. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things, Go Bills!

They can go multiple drives without scoring, and then hit on a big play or three to flip the scoreboard. This should be a lower-scoring game. It probably won’t be fun to watch. sports.title: Royce Lewis Addresses Surprising Trade to Dodgers, Connection to Legend
sports.description: Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Royce Lewis arrived via trade Nov. 20 , and spoke about the whirlwind of emotions he felt after the news. Lewis, the No. 1 overall pick in 2017’s draft, had spent his entire professional career with the Twins, and revealed he was “shocked” after the trade. “Shocked is the word,” Lewis said . “I truly thought I was at least going to have one more year to be the first baseman. I was buying in. … I just wanted to produce for (the fans) and win and be a part of the team that helped get them back into a winning state of mind. I felt like we were starting to turn a corner as an org and going in the right direction. I was just excited to be a part of that movement and that turnaround.” While he wanted to be a part of the Twins’ exciting future, Lewis grew up in Southern California and couldn’t be happier to be putting on the Dodgers’ uniform. “We had our morning coffee and (my wife) randomly said, ‘You’re a Dodger,’” Lewis said . “I was like, ‘What the heck is going on’? It’s almost too good to be true. Especially growing up in Southern California, to be on one of the best teams in the league and close to home, is very special to my family. But it hasn’t sunk in yet.” Additionally, Lewis has a special connection with former Dodgers outfielder Matt Kemp, who gave him his “blessing” to wear No. 27 next season. Apr 2, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Minnesota Twins third baseman Royce Lewis (23) celebrates after hitting a double during the eighth inning against the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images What is Royce Lewis’ Connection With Matt Kemp? Lewis, as a Southern California native, attended Dodger games regularly in his adolescence, and met Kemp at age 10. Lewis said Kemp is the reason he wanted to pursue baseball, and the former Dodgers fan favorite became a mentor to him during his professional career. Kemp texted Lewis following the trade to congratulate him, and Lewis took the opportunity to ask if he could wear his No. 27 next season. Kemp’s response left little room for interpretation. “Heck yeah. Do it. 100%,” Kemp said, per Lewis on AM 570 LA Sports. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Noel Sanchez (@noisebynoel) Kemp played with the Dodgers for 10 seasons, earning three All-Star nods during those seasons as well as two Gold Glove awards and Silver Slugger awards. He finished second in MVP voting in 2011 with a historic season, finishing second behind Ryan Braun, who later admitted to using performance-enhancing drugs that year. Lewis has some big shoes to fill in the No. 27 jersey next season, and will look to live up to those expectations as the Dodgers push to return to the World Series.

technology.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
technology.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. Read full article Comments

A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

technology.title: Hera probe finds DART left a stadium-sized dent in asteroid Dimorphos
technology.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024. DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit. Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits. The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer." Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing. Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts. Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? science.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
science.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos. (Image credit: Ashley Zelinskie) The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time. Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above. Monuments Massimino turned up in our first look at Zelinskie's work, too. In 2022, I photographed the two of them beside her "Exploration JWST" sculpture at "Unfolding the Universe: First Light," an exhibit inspired by the James Webb Space Telescope's first images. Four years later, Massimino stood in a New York gallery looking at another Zelinskie sculpture. "That's my arm there," he told Malik. science.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
science.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Starcloud and Google , in fact, have already launched AI pathfinder satellites.
